column2: The rooftops of Alfama in Lisbon seen from the Miradouro de Santa Luzia: a tiled terrace with blue-and-white azulejo panels and a bougainvillea pergola, terracotta roofs tumbling down the hill to the wide Tagus river, a small yellow vintage tram on a curving lane, a church dome.

Belém Tower in Lisbon: the little white Manueline stone fortress with ornate turrets and arched balconies standing in the Tagus river, gentle water ripples, palm trees and a curving riverside promenade.

The Jerónimos Monastery cloister in Lisbon: two storeys of lace-like carved stone arches around a garden courtyard, with a small plate of Portuguese custard tarts (pastéis de nata) and a coffee cup on a café table in the foreground.

Príncipe Real in Lisbon: a romantic garden square with a giant spreading cedar tree on a trellis, a little fountain, pastel townhouses with wrought-iron balconies and a cozy café kiosk with string lights.
The Roman Temple of Évora in Portugal: tall granite Corinthian columns on a stone podium in a quiet square, whitewashed houses with yellow trim behind, a cathedral tower in the distance.
Monsaraz, Portugal: a medieval whitewashed hilltop village with a castle tower and cobbled lanes, overlooking the great blue Alqueva lake and rolling hills below.

Alentejo countryside in Portugal: rows of vineyards and gnarled cork oak trees over rolling golden hills, a whitewashed country estate with a terracotta roof, a long table set for lunch with wine glasses under a tree.
The Real Alcázar of Seville: an ornate Mudéjar palace courtyard with a long reflecting pool, scalloped arches covered in intricate plasterwork and colorful tiles, sunken gardens with orange trees.

The Santa Cruz quarter of Seville: a narrow whitewashed lane with pots of geraniums on the walls, wrought-iron balconies, an orange tree, and the Giralda bell tower of the cathedral rising above the rooftops.

An intimate candlelit flamenco tablao in Seville: a small wooden stage with a Spanish guitar resting on a chair, a ruffled polka-dot flamenco dress on a dress form, a lace fan and a red rose on a small table, warm lantern light.
Inside the Mezquita-Catedral of Córdoba: an endless forest of columns with double-tiered red-and-white striped horseshoe arches, golden light filtering through.
The Roman Bridge of Córdoba at sunset: long stone arches over the Guadalquivir river, the great Mezquita and its bell tower glowing on the far bank, reeds and water mills in the foreground.
Calleja de las Flores in Córdoba: a tiny whitewashed lane with walls covered in blue flowerpots full of pink geraniums, framing the Mezquita bell tower at the end of the lane.
The Court of the Myrtles in the Alhambra's Nasrid Palaces in Granada: a long reflecting pool lined with myrtle hedges, delicate carved arches and the tall Comares tower mirrored in the water.
The Generalife gardens in Granada: the long water-channel courtyard with arching fountain jets, flower beds and roses, cypress trees, with the Alhambra fortress on the hill behind.

The Alhambra seen from the Mirador de San Nicolás at sunset: the red fortress on its wooded hill glowing, the snow-capped Sierra Nevada mountains behind, whitewashed Albaicín rooftops in the foreground.

A lantern-lit traditional hammam in Granada: an empty Moorish bathhouse with horseshoe arches, star-shaped skylights in a vaulted ceiling, a warm turquoise pool with rose petals floating, brass lanterns and candles.
The Puente Nuevo bridge in Ronda, Spain: the towering stone bridge spanning the deep El Tajo gorge, whitewashed houses perched on the cliff edges, a waterfall in the canyon below.
A pueblo blanco in the mountains of Andalusia: a whitewashed village of cube houses spilling down a hillside around a church and a castle ruin on a rocky crag, olive groves and winding roads.
A mountain vineyard near Ronda, Spain: terraced vines in the hills, a whitewashed cortijo farmhouse, a wine tasting table with two glasses of red wine, a bottle and a cheese board in the foreground.
The Alcazaba of Málaga: a Moorish hillside fortress of terracotta walls, arches and garden courtyards with fountains, overlooking the harbor and the Mediterranean sea.
Muelle Uno waterfront in Málaga: a seaside promenade with palm trees and a white wave-shaped pergola, sailboats in the marina, a lighthouse, the cathedral and the hill fortress behind.
Málaga Cathedral: the grand Renaissance cathedral with its single finished bell tower, palm trees and an orange-tree garden in front.

Wat Phra That Doi Suthep in Chiang Mai, Thailand: the gleaming golden chedi with a golden parasol, temple roofs and bells, on a mountaintop above a misty valley with the city far below, frangipani trees.
Wat Chedi Luang in Chiang Mai: the huge ancient ruined brick chedi with stone naga serpent staircases and elephant sculptures, surrounded by tropical trees, saffron cloth tied around a tree.

A northern Thai cooking class in an open-air garden kitchen in Chiang Mai: a wooden table with a stone mortar and pestle, bowls of curry pastes, chilies, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, fresh herbs and a steaming bowl of khao soi.
An ethical elephant sanctuary in the hills near Chiang Mai: a gentle mother elephant and her baby bathing in a jungle river, lush green hills and bamboo, no saddles or chains.
Wat Rong Khun, the White Temple in Chiang Rai: a dazzling all-white temple with intricate spiky ornaments and mirrored glass inlays, a white bridge over a reflecting pond.
Wat Rong Suea Ten, the Blue Temple in Chiang Rai: a sapphire-blue temple with ornate gold trim and swirling naga serpent sculptures guarding the steps.
The Choui Fong tea plantation in Chiang Rai: neat rows of tea bushes curving over rolling green hills in the mist, a tea pavilion with a glass of iced tea and a teapot in the foreground.
Baan Dam, the Black House in Chiang Rai: dark teak Lanna-style houses with steep peaked roofs and carved buffalo horns in a garden, mysterious and beautiful.

Wat Xieng Thong in Luang Prabang, Laos: the temple with sweeping low layered roofs that nearly touch the ground and a back wall decorated with a glittering glass-mosaic tree of life, frangipani and palms.
Kuang Si Falls near Luang Prabang, Laos: tiered turquoise pools and cascading waterfalls in a lush green forest.
A slow boat on the Mekong river near Luang Prabang: a long wooden river boat with a roof gliding past jungle-covered limestone hills, misty water and a riverside village with stilt houses.
Sunset from Mount Phousi in Luang Prabang: a golden stupa on the hilltop, the town's temple roofs and palm trees below, and the Mekong and Nam Khan rivers winding into the hills.
The Nam Ou river valley at Nong Khiaw, Laos: dramatic steep limestone karst mountains rising straight out of the river, morning mist, a long bridge and a few riverside houses.
A small long-tail boat drifting through a river gorge near Nong Khiaw, Laos: towering karst cliffs draped in jungle, calm green water and a tiny village on the bank.
A cozy riverside bamboo bungalow in Nong Khiaw, Laos: a wooden balcony with a hammock, a book and a cup of tea, looking out over the river at limestone mountains.
Angkor Wat at sunrise in Cambodia: the iconic five lotus-bud towers silhouetted against the dawn sky and reflected in a lotus pond in the foreground.
The Bayon temple at Angkor, Cambodia: stone towers carved with giant serene smiling faces, layered galleries and jungle around.
Ta Prohm temple at Angkor, Cambodia: enormous silk-cotton tree roots pouring over and wrapping around crumbling stone temple walls and a doorway.
Banteay Srei temple in Cambodia: a small exquisite temple of rosy-pink sandstone with intricately carved towers and doorways, a lily pond in front.
